narrative.headline: RBI-KYC-MD 12(a) Tightens High-Risk Customer Review Frequency to Annually
narrative.executive_summary: RBI-KYC-MD clause 12(a) has tightened the required review frequency for high-risk customers from at least once every two years to at least once every year, taking effect on 2025-07-01. This change impacts control KYC-C09 (Periodic KYC Updation - High Risk), owned by the Head of KYC Operations. Customer exposure indicates that 312 out of 1840 accounts (17.0%) are non-compliant at the regulatory period of 365 days. The risk involves two HIGH band design gaps (GAP-0af02e02d12b and GAP-adbf002f08a5) where KYC-C09 only partially meets the updated regulation.
key_risks: KYC-C09 only partially meets RBI-KYC-MD 12(a), creating two HIGH band design gaps (GAP-0af02e02d12b and GAP-adbf002f08a5).
Customer exposure shows 312 out of 1840 accounts (17.0%) are non-compliant at the regulatory period of 365 days.
recommended_next_steps: Head of KYC Operations: Address the partial coverage of KYC-C09 to align with the new annual review requirement under RBI-KYC-MD 12(a).
